tool_input.command:
cd <repo>
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(hooks): join a quote-adjacent word instead of splitting the token (beadle-fc6o)

The tokenizer started a new token at an opening quote unconditionally,
so --git-dir="<path>" became two tokens: "--git-dir=" (the invariant
prefix) and the quoted path interior. "--git-dir=" starts with a dash,
so skip_global_opts treated it as a standalone boolean flag and stepped
past it by one; the actual path then sat as the next token, which is
not "push", so the whole invocation went unclassified and the push was
silently allowed. Confirmed on `git --git-dir="<repo>/.git" push origin
main`, `git -c core.pager="cat" push origin main`, the single-quoted
form, and a bare push whose own --git-dir/--work-tree (both quoted)
redirect it to a repo on main.

Fix the tokenizer's word-boundary rule directly rather than
special-casing `=`: a quote beginning with no whitespace before it
continues the current word, the same way a real shell treats `a"b"c`
as one word. This makes --git-dir="<path>" and -c core.pager="cat"
tokenize identically to their unquoted form.

While rebuilding this path, also close a second gap the same sweep
needed: --git-dir in its `=`-joined form was never captured at all
(is_global_valued only matched the bare token "--git-dir" exactly), and
a bare push's scope resolution had no notion of --git-dir as a scope
target in the first place -- only -C and a preceding cd were tracked.
Added GITDIR capture (both --git-dir <path> and --git-dir=<path> forms,
last one wins) to skip_global_opts, wired it into the PUSH record as a
fifth field, and gave it precedence over -C/cd in the bash-side scope
resolver -- verified against real git that --git-dir directly names the
repository and is authoritative over -C regardless of order.

New cases (jq and no-jq): the four quoted-= deny lines above plus an
unquoted control; git push origin "feat/x" and git push "origin"
feat/x still allow; git -c user.name="A B" push origin feat/x (quoted
value containing a space) still allows. 103 cases, 0 failures (was
87). Header's IMPLEMENTATION section states the word-boundary rule and
the branch check's description now names --git-dir as a scope-resolving
flag alongside -C/cd.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <[redacted-email]>
EOF
)"
